chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who acts with injustice, and the one who supports him, and the one who is pleased with him are partners; all three of them.

key_terms.الْعَامِلُ بِالظُّلْمِ: The one who acts with injustice
key_terms.وَالرَّاضِي بِهِ: And the one who is pleased with it
key_terms.وَالْمُعِينُ لَهُ: And the one who supports him

ai.seo_question: Who shares responsibility for injustice according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to define the tripartite structure of injustice, emphasizing that moral complicity extends beyond the primary actor to include both the facilitator (*al-mu'in*) and the satisfied observer (*al-raḍī*). This classification underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that passive approval and active support are equally culpable in perpetuating systemic wrong, a concept deeply rooted in the broader ethical framework of *Adl* (Justice).
